conflicts.fact: Identity of the gas in the sukuma wiki bubbles
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4: partly CO₂ from respiration plus O₂ from photosynthesis. Lesson 8: O₂ from photosynthesis. Lesson 9: CO₂ from aerobic respiration. Lesson 11: CO₂ from respiration. Lesson 12: both CO₂ and O₂. Students would be taught incompatible answers.

conflicts.fact: Anchoring phenomenon and what the sequence says it is
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and the phenomenon statement: sukuma wiki bubbles in warm vs cold water in Mwalimu Njoroge's Nairobi class. Lesson 5: says the anchoring phenomenon is mandazi dough rising on Mama Wanjiku's counter.

conflicts.fact: Sukuma wiki bubble gas attributed to aerobic respiration vs. anaerobic yeast comparison; also lactic acid in plant roots vs ethanol in plants
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 (reading): anaerobic respiration in plants gives ethanol + CO₂. Lesson 5: plant roots produce lactic acid when waterlogged. Lesson 9: some plant cells produce lactic acid; Lesson 12 says ethanol and CO₂ (or lactate).

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the aerobic/anaerobic equations and model fork were introduced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 refers to 'word equations from Lesson 3' and 'notebooks from Lessons 3–4', but equations were taught in Lesson 4 (Lesson 3 was stomatal mechanisms). Lesson 6 says the aerobic/anaerobic fork was first drawn in Lesson 4, while Lesson 5 says the anaerobic branch was added in Lesson 5.

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which the cumulative model was started
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 4, 7, 8, 12 say the cumulative model started in Lesson 1. Lesson 2 begins building the leaf cross-section model. Lesson 6 says it was started in Lesson 2. Lesson 11 says since Lesson 2.

conflicts.fact: Lesson in which project groups were formed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 10 says groups were formed in Lesson 8, but Lesson 9 is the project launch where groups are formed; Lesson 10 also says plans were from Lesson 9.

Lesson 9: anaerobic respiration tracks (yeast fermentation, biogas, food fermentation). Lesson 10: investigations into plant gas exchange (bubble rate by temperature, stomatal counts, petroleum jelly blocking, CO₂ detection in germinating seeds). Lesson 11: presentations on yeast fermentation, biogas and food fermentation.

conflicts.fact: Whether warm water increases bubbles via stomatal opening vs. enzyme/reaction rates
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 and 3: temperature affects stomatal opening/ion pumping. Lessons 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12: enzyme activity in respiration/photosynthesis.

conflicts.fact: Lesson number references / sukuma wiki climate
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 describes Nairobi as 'temperate highland'; Lesson 9 says sukuma wiki bubbles 'in Lessons 2–5' showed aerobic CO₂ production, although Lesson 2 and 3 attributed them to stomata and Lesson 5 to anaerobic fermentation.

Lesson 2: stomata concentrated on lower epidermis of most leaves, Lesson 2 reading also says upper and lower epidermis; Lesson 7: hydrophyte stomata on upper surface and mesophyte 'moderate arrangement'; Lesson 10 supports more stomata on abaxial surface.
